set — and does not have it deliberately: a document standing above `spec/design/**` cannot be
changed by what stands below it. A lifted item **stays** with its heading and gains a "lifted
by `<CR>`" line together with its former wording; it is never renamed or deleted.

**This route applies to the whole file, not only to the striking-out.** **Every edit to
`spec/invariants.md` within a change cycle** belongs to the convergence round — lifting a
non-goal, adding an invariant, fixing a broken cross-reference. No fan-out author gets this
path in their write set; an author who sees a divergence here **reports it as a finding and
does not try to fix it**. The rule is in this wording because the previous one — written from
a single action — did not catch the second case on the same change.

- **Authentication and authorisation.** There are no accounts, sessions or roles; anybody may
  add, amend and delete anything the system stores: any guestbook entry and any to-do task. The
  signature under an entry is a claim rather than an identity, and no document or screen may assign it a meaning it does not have. A product
  built from this template lifts this non-goal with an ADR and hangs the check on **the router
  aggregate** — once, never per router: a router added later would be left open until somebody
  happened to remember. Which file that is has one home, and it is
  [`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Backend — where a file goes.
Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — this file named the router aggregate by
path, and the path changed when the tree was recut by bounded context; the recut is recorded in
[`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § What a new feature adds, and this document
is edited from the trunk, where no `delta.md` exists in which to call the edit editorial):

- **Update the path and keep it here.** It is the smaller edit and it puts this document back
  in the business of tracking where a file lives — which it would then have to do again on
  every later move. A non-goal is a statement about what the system does not do; the file that
  would enforce it if the non-goal were lifted is a placement fact, and placement facts have
  one home.

- **CSRF protection.** There are no sessions, so there is no cookie or header to forge. This
  project once had a layer that echoed an `X-CSRF-Token` header no service set or checked:
  **it protected nothing and looked to an auditor exactly like protection**. A named non-goal
  is more honest than a stub.
- **Content moderation.** There are no reports, no hiding and no word list.
- **Paging and search.** ~~`GET` returns everything. For an example that is right; `BR-04` has
  already prepared the total order that paging will stand on when it is needed.~~ **Lifted
  outside the SDD process, 2026-08-31**, together with replacing the screen with the mock-up:
  `GET` accepts `q`, `sort`, `limit` and `offset`, and the rule is `BR-05` in
  [`contexts/guestbook.md`](contexts/guestbook.md).

  **The lifting was incomplete for one turn, and that is worth recording.** The rule changed in
  the context, in the contract and in the code, and this item stayed — so a document that binds
  every change was saying something untrue, and no gate caught it. `delta-coverage` holds that a changed
  specification file is covered by a delta; it does not hold that a file which **should**
  change did change. Work outside `/sdd` has no convergence round, which is the only place
  this file may be edited — and that is exactly what was missing.
- **A mobile version.** The screen is a single column up to 860 px and narrows with the
  window, but it is **not designed for a phone**: a mobile view is a separate decision with its
  own requirements, not a scaling of what is there. (Wording corrected 2026-08-31: it spoke of
  a 1440×900 frame, which has not existed since the screen was replaced with the mock-up.)
- **A data retention policy.** An entry, like a to-do task, lives until somebody deletes it. A product storing
  personal data needs a policy here before it can be specified in code.
- **A second database engine.** The application runs on PostgreSQL and only on PostgreSQL
  ([`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § One engine). This is not a lack of
  portability but a refusal to maintain a mode in which a green test says nothing about
  production. A machine without Docker points at its own Postgres; a machine with neither gets
  a **named gap**, not silent green.

## The manual this document cites has moved

The reference tables it points at travel with the process now — the gate register with its retired codes is [the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py) — and not in `docs/`. `docs/` holds
the documentation of the **system** — setting up the AWS account, deploying, configuring,
operating it — and the manual for the **change process** moved beside the framework it
describes.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the rule and its rejected alternatives
live in one place, and this is a pointer to it rather than a second copy; framework changes are
made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): recording the argument again here. See
[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Documentation — where a document goes.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the reference tables moved a second time
on the same day: out of the process's old home here and out of this repository, into the plugin that now
carries the process. The relative links this document used named a path no clone of this
template has. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): restating the
gate names here so this document could stop citing anything. The whole point of the citation is
that the names have one home, and a copy of them here is the drift it exists to prevent.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the reference tables moved a third time,
and this time not by path but by owner: the marketplace that carries them is now in the Scalo
organisation. The absolute links this document used named the organisation it was forked out
of. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): pinning the citations to
that fork because it still answers today. The block above rejected a link into a tree no clone
has; a link into a repository the reader cannot open fails in exactly the same way, one
permission check later.

1	# `contracts/` — system boundaries as versioned contracts
2	
3	A boundary is where this system meets something it does not compile together with itself:
4	somebody else's HTTP client, somebody else's event consumer, yesterday's database state. At
5	a boundary **the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it, not the
6	other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
7	marked `[CRITICAL]`.
8	
9	This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
10	boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.
11	
12	## Why a contract is written rather than generated
13	
14	A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
15	— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
16	repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
17	so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
18	the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
19	had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
20	says how the refusal is declared now).
21	
22	So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
23	output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
24	generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.
25	
26	**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**
27	
28	- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
29	  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
30	  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
31	- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
32	  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
33	  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
34	  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
35	- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
36	  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
37	- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
38	  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
39	  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.
40	
41	The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
42	dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
43	the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
44	would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
45	template that is five paths, ten operations and twelve schemas — and refusals with codes had
46	to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
47	`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.
48	
49	## Compatibility mode
50	
51	A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
52	after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
53	one of three values in its own `README.md`:
54	
55	| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
56	|---|---|
57	| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
58	| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
59	| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |
60	
61	Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
62	code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.
63	
64	## Four boundaries, three directories
65	
66	| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
67	|---|---|
68	| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
69	| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
70	| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
71	| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |
72	
73	**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
74	gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
75	ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
76	the application does not create the schema itself —
77	[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
78	directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
79	first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
80	beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.
81	
82	## What enforces this
83	
84	| Check | What it holds |
85	|---|---|
86	| `contracts` | a file under `contracts/` is hand-written, versioned, and names the check that enforces it |
87	| `delta-coverage` | a contract change is declared in its change's `delta.md` |
88	| `english` | a document under `contracts/` is written in English — as are the fields of the contracts themselves |
89	| `./scripts/contracts.sh` | **the comparison**: every sentence of the HTTP contract is true of the running application |
90	
91	The first three are cheap and textual. The fourth is the one this directory exists for.
92	The full gate table: [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md).

# `contracts/` — system boundaries as versioned contracts

A boundary is where this system meets something it does not compile together with itself:
somebody else's HTTP client, somebody else's event consumer, yesterday's database state. At
a boundary **the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it, not the
other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
marked `[CRITICAL]`.

This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.

## Why a contract is written rather than generated

A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
says how the refusal is declared now).

So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.

**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**

- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.

The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
template that is five paths, ten operations and twelve schemas — and refusals with codes had
to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.

## Compatibility mode

A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
one of three values in its own `README.md`:

| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
|---|---|
| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |

Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.

## Four boundaries, three directories

| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
|---|---|
| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |

**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
the application does not create the schema itself —
[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.

## What enforces this

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `contracts` | a file under `contracts/` is hand-written, versioned, and names the check that enforces it |
| `delta-coverage` | a contract change is declared in its change's `delta.md` |
| `english` | a document under `contracts/` is written in English — as are the fields of the contracts themselves |
| `./scripts/contracts.sh` | **the comparison**: every sentence of the HTTP contract is true of the running application |

The first three are cheap and textual. The fourth is the one this directory exists for.
The full gate table: [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md).

1	# Testing
2	
3	What proves this system works, with which suite and why that one. Where a test file goes and
4	what it is called is stated by [`conventions.md`](conventions.md).
5	
6	## The suites, and what each is for
7	
8	Four tools, four different questions. A suite chosen wrongly is not slower — it is an answer to
9	a different question than the one asked.
10	
11	| Suite | Tool | Asks |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| `tests/unit/` | pytest, no database | whether a pure rule is correct, in seconds |
14	| `tests/integration/` | pytest + Postgres | whether a rule is correct **over real storage** |
15	| `tests/fitness/` | pytest, reads the repo source as text | whether the structure no compiler holds still holds |
16	| `tests/tooling/` | pytest, no database | whether `scripts/` and the e2e harness do what they promise |
17	| `frontend/src/**/*.test.ts` | vitest, node | whether a pure frontend rule is correct |
18	| `frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx` | vitest, jsdom | whether the screen is **wired** to that rule |
19	| `e2e/suite/` | pytest-bdd, a live application | whether the behaviour described in business language actually happens |
20	| `e2e/ui/` | Playwright, Chromium, the built SPA | whether the built application comes up at all and can be used |
21	
22	**Four groups, two pytest suites.** `.specconf/stack.json § suites` declares
23	`fitness` — `tests/fitness/` alone, with its own junit at `.sdd/reports/fitness.junit.xml` —
24	and `backend`, which is the other three groups (`./scripts/test.sh backend` and `--no-db` pass
25	`--ignore=tests/fitness`). They are apart because they answer different questions — a red
26	detector says the structure moved, a red service test says a rule broke — and because the
27	change process attributes a case to exactly one suite: a fitness case collected by both would
28	land in two junits and be read as whichever came last, so a `**Must be red:**` naming a
29	fitness case could not be told from a backend one. `check.sh` runs `Fitness tests` as a gate of
30	its own, before the backend; CI runs it as a step of the `backend` job and on the macOS leg.
31	`tests/fitness/test_gate_parity.py` holds the two suites disjoint and covering every group.
32	
33	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-23, `cr: historical` — the `fitness` suite was declared on the trunk
34	from issue #62 of the 2026-09-20 audit; framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
35	`delta.md`):
36	
37	- **Declare `fitness` and leave `backend` collecting everything.** The smallest diff, and the one
38	  that makes the declaration a lie: every fitness case would sit in both junits, and the process
39	  attributes a case to whichever report it read last, so a red detector could still be filed as
40	  a red backend.
41	- **One suite per group — `unit`, `integration`, `tooling`, `fitness`.** The ticket asked for the
42	  one layer the profile was missing, not for `backend` cut finer. `unit` and `tooling` answer the
43	  same question as `integration` about the product and its tools, and they already have
44	  `test.sh` entry points; only `fitness` asks about the repository instead.
45	- **A CI job of its own for `fitness`.** It needs the backend job's locked environment and
46	  nothing else, so a job would pay for the setup twice. A step with `if: !cancelled()` keeps
47	  its verdict visible when the backend step is red.
48	
49	**The directory is a declaration.** The three database-free groups carry a `conftest.py` that
50	applies `no_db` to everything below, so the marker cannot be forgotten.
51	`tests/fitness/test_test_layout.py` proves the converse: nothing under `tests/integration/`
52	carries `no_db`, because such a test would run on a leg that does not stand up a Postgres and
53	would fail there for a reason unrelated to its subject.
54	
55	## Backend
56	
57	`./scripts/test.sh backend` stands up its own throwaway Postgres through testcontainers. There
58	is no mode in which the suite writes to a developer's database.
59	
60	A test that needs a **fresh** database — because it counts rows or starts from an empty schema —
61	asks for the `fresh_database` fixture. It is the **only place that rebinds `SessionLocal`**, and
62	it rebinds it in every module that holds one, by *discovery* rather than by listing three names.
63	A service added later is then bound automatically; a hand-written list misses it silently, and
64	the symptom is one test's data visible in another, arbitrarily far from the cause.
65	
66	## One machine, one database
67	
68	Postgres is the **only** engine ([`architecture.md`](architecture.md) § One engine), so every
69	test in this suite runs on what production runs on — and a green test says something about it.
70	
71	A machine without Linux Docker is not cut off by this: `APP_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points at a
72	server that machine already has, and the suite creates its own uniquely named, migrated database
73	inside it per run and drops it at the end. The macOS leg in CI takes this route, on a Homebrew
74	Postgres.
75	
76	A machine that has **neither** a daemon **nor** its own Postgres runs the database-free subset
77	(`./scripts/test.sh --no-db`), and `check.sh --no-docker` **names the rest a gap** and exits
78	with code 4. A gate that could not answer is not a gate that passed — and that is the same rule
79	as with `**Verified-by:** manual`: an omission counted and written down is a considered gap, an
80	omission passed over in silence is a gap.
81	
82	The `postgres_only` marker existed while a second engine existed, and it went with it.
83	`tests/fitness/test_test_layout.py` now refuses its return and refuses the removed engine's name
84	in first-party Python — because a second engine does not come back as a decision, but as a
85	branch nobody reviewed as a backend.
86	
87	## What only CI can answer
88	
89	`./scripts/check.sh` is the local definition of "will CI pass" and reproduces almost everything.
90	What it cannot reproduce, named rather than implied:
91	
92	- **The cross-platform leg.** Proof that the suite runs on macOS, and not only on Linux, needs a
93	  macOS machine. CI now answers it weekly, on the trunk, on request, and on a pull request
94	  carrying the `cross-platform` label — not on every pull request, because a macOS runner bills
95	  at 10× on a private plan.
96	- **The specification gates.** They are the change process's, not this application's, and
97	  `check.sh` runs nothing of the process by decision. CI calls them through the composite
98	  action the forge plugin publishes, which supplies the one thing the process's own CI
99	  cannot: a pull request in *this* repository, with its merge base, its draft flag and its
100	  `spec-exempt` label — and the `specs` job recomputes when any of the three moves, because
101	  `ci.yml` fires on `ready_for_review`, `converted_to_draft`, `labeled` and `unlabeled` as
102	  well as on a push. Locally the same verdict comes from `sdd-specs`, which arrives with
103	  the plugin.
104	- **`./scripts/package.sh --lambda`.** The Lambda package resolving for its target platform is
105	  asserted in the `backend` job and has no gate on the local list.
106	- **The image's runtime assertions.** `check.sh` builds the production image; only CI runs it and
107	  checks that it is non-root, ships the SPA, and answers `/api/health` with no database.
108	- **The routing verdict.** `changes` reads the diff to decide what a run could skip, which is a
109	  question that does not exist on a workstation: `check.sh` runs everything, because somebody
110	  asking "will CI pass" is asking about all of it.
111	- **The record of a change made outside the process.** The `changelog` job asks whether *this
112	  pull request* adds an entry under `changelog/`, and reads its base, its author and its labels
113	  to answer. None of the three exists on a workstation. Rejected (decision of 2026-09-14,
114	  `cr: historical` — a local run would have to invent a base, an author and a label set, and a
115	  gate answering a question nobody asked is a gate whose green means nothing): wiring
116	  `./scripts/changelog.sh check` into `check.sh` as a gate. The same command with `--base main`
117	  is there for whoever wants the answer before pushing; it is a question about a branch rather
118	  than a gate over the tree.
119	- **The frontend suite census.** A vitest run that collects zero tests reads on a dashboard
120	  exactly like one that passed, and only CI refuses it — the `frontend` job's
121	  `The frontend suite collected tests` step. `test.sh e2e` has the equivalent for the black box
122	  (`test_sdd_suite_census.py`, run from inside the script, so `check.sh` reaches it) and the
123	  frontend has no such thing. This entry is a **declared gap rather than a design**: moving the
124	  census into `scripts/test.sh frontend` is what Article XII actually asks for, and until that
125	  happens the gap is on this list instead of being a surprise.
126	
127	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — `CI passed` became a required check on
128	2026-09-10, and a metadata run's aggregate replaces the previous one for the same SHA, so a
129	partial run is not a cheaper answer to the same question but an answer to a different one):
130	routing the heavy jobs off a run fired by a pull-request metadata event — leaving a label move
131	or a draft transition to recompute `specs` and `changelog` alone. It would have saved two to
132	three minutes and cost the gate: a pull request with a red `backend` would need only a label
133	added or removed to publish a green required check assembled from the two jobs that did run.
134	Every type on `ci.yml`'s `pull_request` trigger is a full run, and
135	`tests/fitness/test_ci_parity.py` refuses a job that starts branching on
136	`github.event.action`. The saving is available again the day the aggregate can prove that the
137	jobs it did not run were green on this same SHA; until then it is not.
138	
139	## A test that flickers is not a gate
140	
141	**A test whose result varies on an unchanged tree above roughly 2% of runs goes to
142	quarantine before it is allowed to block anything.** Quarantine means: still run, still
143	reported, not on the required check — the same tier `ci-advisory` exists for.
144	
145	The threshold is not the interesting part; the direction is. A gate that fails at random
146	teaches everybody to re-run it, and a re-run reflex is indistinguishable from ignoring the
147	gate — so the first genuine failure after a run of false ones is re-run too. Google operated
148	at roughly 1.5% flakiness and still described it as a burden, which is the scale worth
149	calibrating against: this is not a threshold you clear comfortably.
150	
151	**There is deliberately no `--reruns` here, and no plugin that provides one.** An automatic
152	retry converts a measurement into a silence: the suite goes green and the variability that
153	would have told somebody stops being visible at all. If a test needs a retry to pass, that is
154	the finding. Quarantine it, and fix it or delete it — a test nobody trusts and nobody removes
155	is the worst of the three states.

157	## The JUnit report — who sees it and for how long
158	
159	**A JUnit report may leave the runner as a CI artefact with a retention of no more than 7 days.
160	It may not be committed and its contents may not be printed into a job summary.** This is one
161	rule for all four suites — backend, fitness, frontend and e2e — and it holds in the direction it is
162	written in.
163	
164	The rule exists because for a while the repository said two things at once: a comment beside the
165	backend suite promised the report would **never** become an artefact, while the same workflow
166	uploaded two other JUnit reports with a 7-day retention. An absolute promise that is not applied
167	is worse than a rule with a bound — it teaches that comments beside gates are aspirations.
168	
169	The bound is article XI of the constitution, so two conditions hold and both are checkable:
170	
171	- **Captured output is disabled at the source, not at the reader.** `pyproject.toml` sets
172	  `junit_logging = "no"` for pytest; `frontend/vitest.config.ts` sets
173	  `includeConsoleOutput: false` for vitest's junit reporter. Without the second, the frontend
174	  report carried `<system-out>` **on a green run** — the reporter does that by default.
175	- **Reporter options stand where the reporter is NAMED.** Selecting it from the command line
176	  (`--reporter=junit`) replaces the whole array from the configuration and takes its options with
177	  it, so a flag at the caller silently restores the default behaviour.
178	
179	What remains is the **assertion message**, which no setting removes and which can quote a
180	field's value. Hence 7 days, and hence an artefact rather than a printout: an artefact has an
181	expiry date and requires a login, while a job summary is public and stays.
182	
183	## Coverage is measured and never gated
184	
185	A threshold invites writing lines for the counter, and a line written for the counter proves
186	nothing. A number that **falls** is, however, a suite that has stopped reaching somewhere — and
187	that is a signal worth reading. `--coverage` measures and prints; nothing goes red on the
188	result.

359	  the definition this document gives of a fitness function.
360	- **Leave the header unread and check the same facts by grep in CI.** A grep answers "the string
361	  is there"; it cannot answer "claimed by exactly one context", which is the half that fails in
362	  practice — an orphan and a double claim both read as ordinary text.
363	- **Write no known positives, since the rules hold today.** Every sweep here is vacuously true
364	  with one context and no neighbours, so without them the module would assert nothing and pass
365	  for ever. `test_data_invariants.py` settled this argument first, over a single table.
366	
367	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the process's gate no longer restates
368	`check.sh` gate by gate and no label-parity test compares the two; framework changes are made
369	on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): keeping the mirror. The gate now calls `check.sh` by the
370	name the script contract fixes and reads the suites' junits it leaves behind
371	(the process's `script-contract.md`), so "the gate is CI" holds by construction; what the
372	template still owes the contract — the three-state exit, the junit path, the executable bit —
373	is proved here by `test_gate_parity.py`, from the template's own files and without importing
374	the process. Also rejected: proving those three things from the process's side, which would
375	make the template's tests depend on the process — the direction the split forbids.
376	
377	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — `test_scripts_discipline.py` allowed
378	exactly one script to commit, and the script that did can no longer do it, so the rule is
379	amended here rather than left describing a repository that does not exist; framework changes
380	are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
381	
382	- **Keep "one script commits, and it is `release.sh`".** It described a release that wrote a
383	  version into `pyproject.toml` and put the result on the trunk. The branch ruleset refuses
384	  that push to everybody — `bypass_actors` is empty — so the allowance covered something that
385	  could not happen, and the commit it allowed left `uv.lock` naming the version before it.
386	  A release now tags a commit a pull request already put there. Allowing a commit nothing
387	  makes is an exemption waiting to be used by the next script that wants one.
388	- **Drop the commit half and police only the push.** The detector would then be silent about
389	  the thing that caused the incident this test exists for — three commit conventions side by
390	  side — and a rule that once had a reason reads as arbitrary the moment its reason is
391	  deleted rather than tightened.
392	
393	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — the CloudFront edge was rewriting the API's
394	own refusals into `200 text/html`, and no suite in this repository could have seen it, so the
395	table gains `test_edge_contract.py`; the repair was made on the trunk and carries no `delta.md`
396	in which to declare the edit):
397	
398	- **Put the assertions in `test_infra_layout.py`.** That file is about the Terraform **roots** —
399	  which ones exist, what they pin, which state key they hold — and an edge behaviour is a
400	  property of one module's inside. A file that guards a shape and also guards a rule is the
401	  `utils.py` of test modules: the next unrelated rule goes there too, because it already went
402	  there once.
403	- **Pin nothing, and rely on the issue's acceptance criteria.** Those are measured through a
404	  live distribution, which is the honest way to prove the behaviour and no way at all to stop
405	  the configuration coming back — the two `custom_error_response` blocks would have returned
406	  through a green suite. **The gap is named rather than closed:** what is checked here is the
407	  configuration, and the behaviour is confirmed on the next apply.
408	
409	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — three labels decide what CI does and two of
410	them did not exist, so the table gains `test_label_registry.py`; a label is a repository setting
411	and the repair was made on the trunk, so it carries no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
412	
413	- **Ask the GitHub API whether the labels exist.** It is the question that actually went
414	  unanswered, and it is the one this suite may not ask: every module here runs with no network
415	  and no token (`tests/fitness/conftest.py`), so such a test would be red on an aeroplane, red
416	  on a fork, and green only where a credential happened to be. **The gap is named rather than
417	  closed:** what is checked is that the register and the automation agree on the names, and
418	  `.github/labels.md` carries a dated claim, re-checkable in one `gh` command, for the rest.
419	- **Check it in CI instead, where a token exists.** That buys the real answer and spends the
420	  property that makes this directory worth having: a fitness function answers the same on a
421	  workstation as in a run, which is why an author can see the rule before a reviewer does. A
422	  check only CI can run belongs in § What only CI can answer, and this one is not worth a job.
423	- **Keep the labels in the modules that read them.** `changelog.sh` knows its own arm and
424	  `ci.yml` knows its own `if:`, and neither can know it is the last reader of a name nothing
425	  created. The register exists because the fact is about the repository rather than about
426	  either file, and a fact split between two files is the one nobody owns.
427	- **Assert the number of labels.** The first draft did, and it would have turned red on the
428	  correct act of retiring one. What is asserted is that no row is skipped by the parser — the
429	  failure that would make every other rule here vacuous.
430	
431	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — every `uses:` in the five workflows ran a
432	mutable tag, so the table gains `test_action_pins.py`; the repair was made on the trunk against
433	issue #31 and carries no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
434	
435	- **Rely on the engine's `ci_meta.check_pins`.** It states the same rule, and it has never read a
436	  line of this repository: its `github_dir()` walks up from the **plugin's** own root, so it
437	  judges the tree the process ships from. A rule enforced somewhere else, over somebody else's
438	  files, is a rule this repository does not have — and the 47 unpinned steps are what that reads
439	  like from here.
440	- **Put the assertions in `test_ci_parity.py`.** It already opens `ci.yml`, which is exactly the
441	  argument that makes it the wrong home: that file is about the **map between gates and jobs**,
442	  and a pin is a property of one step. The same reasoning `test_edge_contract.py` records against
443	  `test_infra_layout.py` above — a file that guards a shape and also guards a rule is the
444	  `utils.py` of test modules.
445	- **Pin the process's two composite actions along with the rest.** `ci.yml` argues `@main` where
446	  it uses them and `CLAUDE.md` makes "live the moment they merge there" a property rather than an
447	  oversight; pinning would have traded a reviewed decision for a pin-bump pull request per engine
448	  release. They are **named in the module with their reason**, and the list clears itself when a
449	  reference stops being used — which is the difference between a decision and a blind spot.
450	
451	## The reference corpus (golden set)
452	
453	`golden-set/` is the only home of committed data this project ships, and it is **cut in two by
454	what the data is for**. What each half is, and what it owes, is
455	[`golden-set/README.md`](../../golden-set/README.md); what belongs to testing is here.
456	
457	| Half | What it is | Read by | Lifetime |
458	|---|---|---|---|
459	| `golden-set/fixtures/` | what the suites read instead of inventing | pytest, the black box | wiped before every scenario |
460	| `golden-set/seed/` | what a freshly created environment opens with | `scripts/seed_golden_set.py` | the life of the environment |
461	
462	The seeder reads the **boundary fixture too**, and only under `./scripts/seed.sh --boundary`,
463	when somebody asks for a preview that shows the limits. That is the one crossing between the
464	halves and it is deliberate (`golden-set/README.md` § Rules only `fixtures/` obeys); it means
465	the fixture half has a second reader whose reason to change lives outside the test suites.
466	
467	**Only the fixture half is a testing artefact.** The seed half is an environment's initial
468	state and is specified in [`architecture.md`](architecture.md) § What a new environment starts
469	with. It is named here because for a while it was not named anywhere: the seeder posted
470	`entries-ordinary.json`, this section said the corpus had two readers, and both statements were
471	about the same three files.
472	
473	**No suite asserts about the seed half, and `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` enforces it.**
474	A test that reaches for it makes the two halves one corpus again under two directory names:
475	the seed data could then no longer change for the reason it exists — to make a screen worth
476	judging — without reddening a suite. That is the coupling the split removed, and the rule is a
477	check rather than a convention because it was rediscovered rather than foreseen.
478	
479	### The fixture half
480	
481	Each file has one story:
482	
483	| File | Story | Read by |
484	|---|---|---|
485	| `entries-ordinary.json` | ordinary entries in **writing** order — non-ASCII characters, a multi-line message, single-character entries | `test_guestbook_entries_corpus.py`, the e2e scenarios |
486	| `entries-boundary.json` | values **exactly** on the bound, each of which must be accepted | as above |
487	| `entries-refused.json` | entries the rules refuse, each with a refusal code | as above |
488	| `text-measurement.json` | how a field is trimmed and how long it is — **cases, not entries** | `test_entry_text_rules.py` **and** `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/entryText.test.ts` |
489	| `todo-tasks-ordinary.json` | ordinary tasks in **adding** order, each with its done mark — a repeated text, characters outside ASCII, a one-character task, no line break anywhere | `test_todo_tasks_corpus.py` |
490	| `todo-tasks-boundary.json` | task texts **exactly** on the bound — ASCII, emoji, decomposed letters, padded with spaces — and the one-character minimum, each of which must be accepted, with the text it is stored as | as above |
491	| `todo-tasks-refused.json` | task texts the rules refuse, each naming the refusal code it expects (`todo_task_text_empty`, `todo_task_text_too_long`, `todo_task_text_multiline`), over the bound by exactly one code point | as above |
492	| `todo-task-text.json` | how a task's text is judged — the bound in code points and the seven line breaks — **cases, not tasks**, with a fourth verdict, `multiline`, beside `accepted`, `empty` and `too_long` | `test_todo_task_text_rules.py` **and** the to-do list's browser rule test (§ Evidence map, `CR-2609-823a`) |
493	
494	**Two files in that table are read by the browser, each by exactly one module of the context
495	whose rule it proves.** Every other fixture
496	is sized by what the server must prove, so a component asserting against one acquires a
497	dependency whose reasons to change live in another suite. `text-measurement.json` is sized by
498	what the two sides must AGREE about — and a claim about agreement cannot be checked from one
499	side, while a second copy beside the browser's test would be two lists nothing holds equal.
500	`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` names the one module that may read it and refuses every
501	other file in `frontend/src` exactly as before; `golden-set/README.md` § The frontend carries
502	the reasoning.
503	
504	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-17, `cr: historical` — where the shared corpus lives and what
505	binds the two sides, decided on GitHub issue #28, outside `/forge:sdd`):
506	
507	- **Put the corpus under `contracts/` instead, where no rule forbids the frontend to read it.**
508	  It is defensible — the file does describe a boundary — and it costs more than it saves:
509	  `contracts/<kind>/<area>.yaml|.md` admits no `.json`, a new subdirectory owes a `README.md`
510	  with a declared compatibility mode, and the `english` gate's non-ASCII exemption names
511	  `golden-set/` and nothing else. Three documents would have had to move so that one fitness
512	  rule need not gain one named exception.
513	- **Give each language its own copy, held equal by a fitness test.** It is the shape this
514	  repository already uses for the length constants — and it is the shape that produced the
515	  defect. A test can compare two literals; it cannot compare what two languages do with them.
516	- **Keep `test_length_constants.py` as the only binding and widen its assertions.** It reads the
517	  TypeScript as text with a regular expression. It can see that a literal is `80`; there is no
518	  extension of it that can see what `.length` counts.
519	
520	**`todo-task-text.json` is the same kind of file for the to-do list's own rule** — the bound of
521	200 code points and the seven line breaks of `BR-07` — and it is read the same way: by
522	`test_todo_task_text_rules.py` on the server and by exactly one module in the to-do list's
523	browser folder, against the same bytes, asserting the same verdicts and the same lengths. It
524	carries only what the to-do list adds to the shared text rule. How a text is normalized, trimmed
525	and counted stays proved by `text-measurement.json` alone: a task's text calls that one rule
526	(`spec/contexts/todo_list.md` § Neighbours), so its thirteen single-whitespace cases need no
527	copy. The task files are named `todo-task…`, never a bare `task`, for the reason
528	[`../glossary.md`](../glossary.md) § Task (process) gives; the names replace the `tasks-*.json`
529	that `CR-2609-823a`'s `scenarios.md` § Test data proposed, and every value it gives them stands.
530	
531	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-24, `CR-2609-823a` — where the to-do list's text cases live and
532	who reads them in the browser, which `scenarios.md` § Test data left to the design):
533	
534	- **Add the task's cases to `text-measurement.json`, as `scenarios.md` proposed.** Its three
535	  readers look each case's field up in a table of bounds that has no task field, so the commit
536	  that added the cases would turn existing guestbook cases red on both sides, while the frontend
537	  test author runs beside the fixture author and is told to stop on any existing red. Its
538	  fitness sweeps would have to import the task's bound from a module that does not exist until
539	  the implementation, and a failed import at the top of a module un-collects every case in it.
540	  And the file is deleted with the guestbook (`CLAUDE.md` § What is an example): the to-do list
541	  would lose the proof of its own rule along with somebody else's example.
542	- **Let the one browser module that reads `text-measurement.json` read the task's cases too.** A
543	  reader of both contexts' verdicts needs both contexts' bounds. The guestbook's reader may not
544	  import the to-do list's folder, and no module outside the contexts may import either, the
545	  composition root `frontend/src/router.tsx` aside (`tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py`).
546	- **Give the to-do list's browser test its own inline copy of the cases.** It is the defect
547	  `D-04` records, one context over: two lists that have to stay equal and nothing making them.
548	
549	**The fixture half is a feeder for parametrisation, not a set of files to look at.** A test
550	takes all its cases at once (`pytest.mark.parametrize`), and a Gherkin scenario takes one **by
551	the sentence** the corpus carries for it. That is what lets a `.feature` say `the signature is
552	all spaces` rather than `author_whitespace_only`, with no second list that has to agree with the
553	corpus.
554	
555	**Bounds are computed from the model's constants, never transcribed.** The boundary file was
556	produced from `AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` and `MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH`, and
557	`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` checks that agreement on every run — so moving a rule reddens
558	the corpus instead of silently invalidating it. The to-do list's boundary and refused files are
559	held to `TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH` the same way, and never to `QUERY_MAX_LENGTH`: the search
560	phrase is also bounded at 200, and a test that reads the phrase's constant to prove the task's
561	bound proves the wrong rule.
562	
563	**The order in `entries-ordinary.json` is WRITING order.** The list returns the reverse
564	(`BR-04`), and the test asserts **the reversal of the file** rather than a hand-written list —
565	because the first is a claim about a rule and the second is a second copy of the data.
566	`todo-tasks-ordinary.json` is in ADDING order and states each task's done mark: its reader adds
567	every task in file order and only then marks the done ones, because a new task is never born
568	done (`BR-08`), and asserts the reversal of the file with the marks it states (`BR-11`).
569	
570	**Hostile input does not belong in the corpus.** The boundary runs where what a guest could
571	really send ends: a signature of nothing but spaces **belongs** (that happens), while bytes
572	built to break a parser do not. Those live in the test's code, beside the assertion that
573	explains them.
574	
575	**The frontend reads neither half.** Component fixtures are synthetic and written on the
576	spot: a component test that needs committed reference data is a test asking a question about the
577	corpus. Two suites read the fixture half — pytest and the black box — and `seed_golden_set.py`
578	reads the seed half always and the boundary fixture on request.
579	
580	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-05, `cr: historical` — both corrections were found by auditing
581	this document against the code it describes, on the trunk, where `spec/ADR/` is not yet open
582	and there is no `delta.md` to declare an edit editorial in):
583	
584	- **Remove `seed.sh --boundary` so the sentence becomes true again.** It is the cheaper
585	  sentence and the worse product: the flag exists so a person can raise a preview that shows
586	  the limits, which is exactly when a reviewer wants to see them. The coupling it creates is
587	  real and belongs in this document rather than being designed away to keep a table tidy.
588	- **Make the two fitness modules stop importing `app`.** That means transcribing
589	  `AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` and `MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH` into the tests — which is the exact practice
590	  § Bounds are read from the constant forbids two sections below, and which
591	  `test_length_constants.py` exists to catch.
592	- **Say nothing and let the preamble stand.** It is the sentence a reader uses to decide
593	  whether a new fitness test may import the application. Wrong, it answers "no" to a question
594	  the tree answers "yes" to twice.
595	
596	### The black box owns the database it runs against
597

# Testing

What proves this system works, with which suite and why that one. Where a test file goes and
what it is called is stated by [`conventions.md`](conventions.md).

## The suites, and what each is for

Four tools, four different questions. A suite chosen wrongly is not slower — it is an answer to
a different question than the one asked.

| Suite | Tool | Asks |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/unit/` | pytest, no database | whether a pure rule is correct, in seconds |
| `tests/integration/` | pytest + Postgres | whether a rule is correct **over real storage** |
| `tests/fitness/` | pytest, reads the repo source as text | whether the structure no compiler holds still holds |
| `tests/tooling/` | pytest, no database | whether `scripts/` and the e2e harness do what they promise |
| `frontend/src/**/*.test.ts` | vitest, node | whether a pure frontend rule is correct |
| `frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx` | vitest, jsdom | whether the screen is **wired** to that rule |
| `e2e/suite/` | pytest-bdd, a live application | whether the behaviour described in business language actually happens |
| `e2e/ui/` | Playwright, Chromium, the built SPA | whether the built application comes up at all and can be used |

**Four groups, two pytest suites.** `.specconf/stack.json § suites` declares
`fitness` — `tests/fitness/` alone, with its own junit at `.sdd/reports/fitness.junit.xml` —
and `backend`, which is the other three groups (`./scripts/test.sh backend` and `--no-db` pass
`--ignore=tests/fitness`). They are apart because they answer different questions — a red
detector says the structure moved, a red service test says a rule broke — and because the
change process attributes a case to exactly one suite: a fitness case collected by both would
land in two junits and be read as whichever came last, so a `**Must be red:**` naming a
fitness case could not be told from a backend one. `check.sh` runs `Fitness tests` as a gate of
its own, before the backend; CI runs it as a step of the `backend` job and on the macOS leg.
`tests/fitness/test_gate_parity.py` holds the two suites disjoint and covering every group.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-23, `cr: historical` — the `fitness` suite was declared on the trunk
from issue #62 of the 2026-09-20 audit; framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
`delta.md`):

- **Declare `fitness` and leave `backend` collecting everything.** The smallest diff, and the one
  that makes the declaration a lie: every fitness case would sit in both junits, and the process
  attributes a case to whichever report it read last, so a red detector could still be filed as
  a red backend.
- **One suite per group — `unit`, `integration`, `tooling`, `fitness`.** The ticket asked for the
  one layer the profile was missing, not for `backend` cut finer. `unit` and `tooling` answer the
  same question as `integration` about the product and its tools, and they already have
  `test.sh` entry points; only `fitness` asks about the repository instead.
- **A CI job of its own for `fitness`.** It needs the backend job's locked environment and
  nothing else, so a job would pay for the setup twice. A step with `if: !cancelled()` keeps
  its verdict visible when the backend step is red.

**The directory is a declaration.** The three database-free groups carry a `conftest.py` that
applies `no_db` to everything below, so the marker cannot be forgotten.
`tests/fitness/test_test_layout.py` proves the converse: nothing under `tests/integration/`
carries `no_db`, because such a test would run on a leg that does not stand up a Postgres and
would fail there for a reason unrelated to its subject.

## Backend

`./scripts/test.sh backend` stands up its own throwaway Postgres through testcontainers. There
is no mode in which the suite writes to a developer's database.

A test that needs a **fresh** database — because it counts rows or starts from an empty schema —
asks for the `fresh_database` fixture. It is the **only place that rebinds `SessionLocal`**, and
it rebinds it in every module that holds one, by *discovery* rather than by listing three names.
A service added later is then bound automatically; a hand-written list misses it silently, and
the symptom is one test's data visible in another, arbitrarily far from the cause.

## One machine, one database

Postgres is the **only** engine ([`architecture.md`](architecture.md) § One engine), so every
test in this suite runs on what production runs on — and a green test says something about it.

A machine without Linux Docker is not cut off by this: `APP_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points at a
server that machine already has, and the suite creates its own uniquely named, migrated database
inside it per run and drops it at the end. The macOS leg in CI takes this route, on a Homebrew
Postgres.

A machine that has **neither** a daemon **nor** its own Postgres runs the database-free subset
(`./scripts/test.sh --no-db`), and `check.sh --no-docker` **names the rest a gap** and exits
with code 4. A gate that could not answer is not a gate that passed — and that is the same rule
as with `**Verified-by:** manual`: an omission counted and written down is a considered gap, an
omission passed over in silence is a gap.

The `postgres_only` marker existed while a second engine existed, and it went with it.
`tests/fitness/test_test_layout.py` now refuses its return and refuses the removed engine's name
in first-party Python — because a second engine does not come back as a decision, but as a
branch nobody reviewed as a backend.

## What only CI can answer

`./scripts/check.sh` is the local definition of "will CI pass" and reproduces almost everything.
What it cannot reproduce, named rather than implied:

- **The cross-platform leg.** Proof that the suite runs on macOS, and not only on Linux, needs a
  macOS machine. CI now answers it weekly, on the trunk, on request, and on a pull request
  carrying the `cross-platform` label — not on every pull request, because a macOS runner bills
  at 10× on a private plan.
- **The specification gates.** They are the change process's, not this application's, and
  `check.sh` runs nothing of the process by decision. CI calls them through the composite
  action the forge plugin publishes, which supplies the one thing the process's own CI
  cannot: a pull request in *this* repository, with its merge base, its draft flag and its
  `spec-exempt` label — and the `specs` job recomputes when any of the three moves, because
  `ci.yml` fires on `ready_for_review`, `converted_to_draft`, `labeled` and `unlabeled` as
  well as on a push. Locally the same verdict comes from `sdd-specs`, which arrives with
  the plugin.
- **`./scripts/package.sh --lambda`.** The Lambda package resolving for its target platform is
  asserted in the `backend` job and has no gate on the local list.
- **The image's runtime assertions.** `check.sh` builds the production image; only CI runs it and
  checks that it is non-root, ships the SPA, and answers `/api/health` with no database.
- **The routing verdict.** `changes` reads the diff to decide what a run could skip, which is a
  question that does not exist on a workstation: `check.sh` runs everything, because somebody
  asking "will CI pass" is asking about all of it.
- **The record of a change made outside the process.** The `changelog` job asks whether *this
  pull request* adds an entry under `changelog/`, and reads its base, its author and its labels
  to answer. None of the three exists on a workstation. Rejected (decision of 2026-09-14,
  `cr: historical` — a local run would have to invent a base, an author and a label set, and a
  gate answering a question nobody asked is a gate whose green means nothing): wiring
  `./scripts/changelog.sh check` into `check.sh` as a gate. The same command with `--base main`
  is there for whoever wants the answer before pushing; it is a question about a branch rather
  than a gate over the tree.
- **The frontend suite census.** A vitest run that collects zero tests reads on a dashboard
  exactly like one that passed, and only CI refuses it — the `frontend` job's
  `The frontend suite collected tests` step. `test.sh e2e` has the equivalent for the black box
  (`test_sdd_suite_census.py`, run from inside the script, so `check.sh` reaches it) and the
  frontend has no such thing. This entry is a **declared gap rather than a design**: moving the
  census into `scripts/test.sh frontend` is what Article XII actually asks for, and until that
  happens the gap is on this list instead of being a surprise.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — `CI passed` became a required check on
2026-09-10, and a metadata run's aggregate replaces the previous one for the same SHA, so a
partial run is not a cheaper answer to the same question but an answer to a different one):
routing the heavy jobs off a run fired by a pull-request metadata event — leaving a label move
or a draft transition to recompute `specs` and `changelog` alone. It would have saved two to
three minutes and cost the gate: a pull request with a red `backend` would need only a label
added or removed to publish a green required check assembled from the two jobs that did run.
Every type on `ci.yml`'s `pull_request` trigger is a full run, and
`tests/fitness/test_ci_parity.py` refuses a job that starts branching on
`github.event.action`. The saving is available again the day the aggregate can prove that the
jobs it did not run were green on this same SHA; until then it is not.

## A test that flickers is not a gate

**A test whose result varies on an unchanged tree above roughly 2% of runs goes to
quarantine before it is allowed to block anything.** Quarantine means: still run, still
reported, not on the required check — the same tier `ci-advisory` exists for.

The threshold is not the interesting part; the direction is. A gate that fails at random
teaches everybody to re-run it, and a re-run reflex is indistinguishable from ignoring the
gate — so the first genuine failure after a run of false ones is re-run too. Google operated
at roughly 1.5% flakiness and still described it as a burden, which is the scale worth
calibrating against: this is not a threshold you clear comfortably.

**There is deliberately no `--reruns` here, and no plugin that provides one.** An automatic
retry converts a measurement into a silence: the suite goes green and the variability that
would have told somebody stops being visible at all. If a test needs a retry to pass, that is
the finding. Quarantine it, and fix it or delete it — a test nobody trusts and nobody removes
is the worst of the three states.

## The JUnit report — who sees it and for how long

**A JUnit report may leave the runner as a CI artefact with a retention of no more than 7 days.
It may not be committed and its contents may not be printed into a job summary.** This is one
rule for all four suites — backend, fitness, frontend and e2e — and it holds in the direction it is
written in.

The rule exists because for a while the repository said two things at once: a comment beside the
backend suite promised the report would **never** become an artefact, while the same workflow
uploaded two other JUnit reports with a 7-day retention. An absolute promise that is not applied
is worse than a rule with a bound — it teaches that comments beside gates are aspirations.

The bound is article XI of the constitution, so two conditions hold and both are checkable:

- **Captured output is disabled at the source, not at the reader.** `pyproject.toml` sets
  `junit_logging = "no"` for pytest; `frontend/vitest.config.ts` sets
  `includeConsoleOutput: false` for vitest's junit reporter. Without the second, the frontend
  report carried `<system-out>` **on a green run** — the reporter does that by default.
- **Reporter options stand where the reporter is NAMED.** Selecting it from the command line
  (`--reporter=junit`) replaces the whole array from the configuration and takes its options with
  it, so a flag at the caller silently restores the default behaviour.

What remains is the **assertion message**, which no setting removes and which can quote a
field's value. Hence 7 days, and hence an artefact rather than a printout: an artefact has an
expiry date and requires a login, while a job summary is public and stays.

## Coverage is measured and never gated

A threshold invites writing lines for the counter, and a line written for the counter proves
nothing. A number that **falls** is, however, a suite that has stopped reaching somewhere — and
that is a signal worth reading. `--coverage` measures and prints; nothing goes red on the
result.

## The reference corpus (golden set)

`golden-set/` is the only home of committed data this project ships, and it is **cut in two by
what the data is for**. What each half is, and what it owes, is
[`golden-set/README.md`](../../golden-set/README.md); what belongs to testing is here.

| Half | What it is | Read by | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| `golden-set/fixtures/` | what the suites read instead of inventing | pytest, the black box | wiped before every scenario |
| `golden-set/seed/` | what a freshly created environment opens with | `scripts/seed_golden_set.py` | the life of the environment |

The seeder reads the **boundary fixture too**, and only under `./scripts/seed.sh --boundary`,
when somebody asks for a preview that shows the limits. That is the one crossing between the
halves and it is deliberate (`golden-set/README.md` § Rules only `fixtures/` obeys); it means
the fixture half has a second reader whose reason to change lives outside the test suites.

**Only the fixture half is a testing artefact.** The seed half is an environment's initial
state and is specified in [`architecture.md`](architecture.md) § What a new environment starts
with. It is named here because for a while it was not named anywhere: the seeder posted
`entries-ordinary.json`, this section said the corpus had two readers, and both statements were
about the same three files.

**No suite asserts about the seed half, and `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` enforces it.**
A test that reaches for it makes the two halves one corpus again under two directory names:
the seed data could then no longer change for the reason it exists — to make a screen worth
judging — without reddening a suite. That is the coupling the split removed, and the rule is a
check rather than a convention because it was rediscovered rather than foreseen.

### The fixture half

Each file has one story:

| File | Story | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `entries-ordinary.json` | ordinary entries in **writing** order — non-ASCII characters, a multi-line message, single-character entries | `test_guestbook_entries_corpus.py`, the e2e scenarios |
| `entries-boundary.json` | values **exactly** on the bound, each of which must be accepted | as above |
| `entries-refused.json` | entries the rules refuse, each with a refusal code | as above |
| `text-measurement.json` | how a field is trimmed and how long it is — **cases, not entries** | `test_entry_text_rules.py` **and** `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/entryText.test.ts` |
| `todo-tasks-ordinary.json` | ordinary tasks in **adding** order, each with its done mark — a repeated text, characters outside ASCII, a one-character task, no line break anywhere | `test_todo_tasks_corpus.py` |
| `todo-tasks-boundary.json` | task texts **exactly** on the bound — ASCII, emoji, decomposed letters, padded with spaces — and the one-character minimum, each of which must be accepted, with the text it is stored as | as above |
| `todo-tasks-refused.json` | task texts the rules refuse, each naming the refusal code it expects (`todo_task_text_empty`, `todo_task_text_too_long`, `todo_task_text_multiline`), over the bound by exactly one code point | as above |
| `todo-task-text.json` | how a task's text is judged — the bound in code points and the seven line breaks — **cases, not tasks**, with a fourth verdict, `multiline`, beside `accepted`, `empty` and `too_long` | `test_todo_task_text_rules.py` **and** the to-do list's browser rule test (§ Evidence map, `CR-2609-823a`) |

**Two files in that table are read by the browser, each by exactly one module of the context
whose rule it proves.** Every other fixture
is sized by what the server must prove, so a component asserting against one acquires a
dependency whose reasons to change live in another suite. `text-measurement.json` is sized by
what the two sides must AGREE about — and a claim about agreement cannot be checked from one
side, while a second copy beside the browser's test would be two lists nothing holds equal.
`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` names the one module that may read it and refuses every
other file in `frontend/src` exactly as before; `golden-set/README.md` § The frontend carries
the reasoning.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-17, `cr: historical` — where the shared corpus lives and what
binds the two sides, decided on GitHub issue #28, outside `/forge:sdd`):

- **Put the corpus under `contracts/` instead, where no rule forbids the frontend to read it.**
  It is defensible — the file does describe a boundary — and it costs more than it saves:
  `contracts/<kind>/<area>.yaml|.md` admits no `.json`, a new subdirectory owes a `README.md`
  with a declared compatibility mode, and the `english` gate's non-ASCII exemption names
  `golden-set/` and nothing else. Three documents would have had to move so that one fitness
  rule need not gain one named exception.
- **Give each language its own copy, held equal by a fitness test.** It is the shape this
  repository already uses for the length constants — and it is the shape that produced the
  defect. A test can compare two literals; it cannot compare what two languages do with them.
- **Keep `test_length_constants.py` as the only binding and widen its assertions.** It reads the
  TypeScript as text with a regular expression. It can see that a literal is `80`; there is no
  extension of it that can see what `.length` counts.

**`todo-task-text.json` is the same kind of file for the to-do list's own rule** — the bound of
200 code points and the seven line breaks of `BR-07` — and it is read the same way: by
`test_todo_task_text_rules.py` on the server and by exactly one module in the to-do list's
browser folder, against the same bytes, asserting the same verdicts and the same lengths. It
carries only what the to-do list adds to the shared text rule. How a text is normalized, trimmed
and counted stays proved by `text-measurement.json` alone: a task's text calls that one rule
(`spec/contexts/todo_list.md` § Neighbours), so its thirteen single-whitespace cases need no
copy. The task files are named `todo-task…`, never a bare `task`, for the reason
[`../glossary.md`](../glossary.md) § Task (process) gives; the names replace the `tasks-*.json`
that `CR-2609-823a`'s `scenarios.md` § Test data proposed, and every value it gives them stands.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-24, `CR-2609-823a` — where the to-do list's text cases live and
who reads them in the browser, which `scenarios.md` § Test data left to the design):

- **Add the task's cases to `text-measurement.json`, as `scenarios.md` proposed.** Its three
  readers look each case's field up in a table of bounds that has no task field, so the commit
  that added the cases would turn existing guestbook cases red on both sides, while the frontend
  test author runs beside the fixture author and is told to stop on any existing red. Its
  fitness sweeps would have to import the task's bound from a module that does not exist until
  the implementation, and a failed import at the top of a module un-collects every case in it.
  And the file is deleted with the guestbook (`CLAUDE.md` § What is an example): the to-do list
  would lose the proof of its own rule along with somebody else's example.
- **Let the one browser module that reads `text-measurement.json` read the task's cases too.** A
  reader of both contexts' verdicts needs both contexts' bounds. The guestbook's reader may not
  import the to-do list's folder, and no module outside the contexts may import either, the
  composition root `frontend/src/router.tsx` aside (`tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py`).
- **Give the to-do list's browser test its own inline copy of the cases.** It is the defect
  `D-04` records, one context over: two lists that have to stay equal and nothing making them.

**The fixture half is a feeder for parametrisation, not a set of files to look at.** A test
takes all its cases at once (`pytest.mark.parametrize`), and a Gherkin scenario takes one **by
the sentence** the corpus carries for it. That is what lets a `.feature` say `the signature is
all spaces` rather than `author_whitespace_only`, with no second list that has to agree with the
corpus.

**Bounds are computed from the model's constants, never transcribed.** The boundary file was
produced from `AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` and `MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH`, and
`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` checks that agreement on every run — so moving a rule reddens
the corpus instead of silently invalidating it. The to-do list's boundary and refused files are
held to `TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH` the same way, and never to `QUERY_MAX_LENGTH`: the search
phrase is also bounded at 200, and a test that reads the phrase's constant to prove the task's
bound proves the wrong rule.

**The order in `entries-ordinary.json` is WRITING order.** The list returns the reverse
(`BR-04`), and the test asserts **the reversal of the file** rather than a hand-written list —
because the first is a claim about a rule and the second is a second copy of the data.
`todo-tasks-ordinary.json` is in ADDING order and states each task's done mark: its reader adds
every task in file order and only then marks the done ones, because a new task is never born
done (`BR-08`), and asserts the reversal of the file with the marks it states (`BR-11`).

**Hostile input does not belong in the corpus.** The boundary runs where what a guest could
really send ends: a signature of nothing but spaces **belongs** (that happens), while bytes
built to break a parser do not. Those live in the test's code, beside the assertion that
explains them.

**The frontend reads neither half.** Component fixtures are synthetic and written on the
spot: a component test that needs committed reference data is a test asking a question about the
corpus. Two suites read the fixture half — pytest and the black box — and `seed_golden_set.py`
reads the seed half always and the boundary fixture on request.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-05, `cr: historical` — both corrections were found by auditing
this document against the code it describes, on the trunk, where `spec/ADR/` is not yet open
and there is no `delta.md` to declare an edit editorial in):

- **Remove `seed.sh --boundary` so the sentence becomes true again.** It is the cheaper
  sentence and the worse product: the flag exists so a person can raise a preview that shows
  the limits, which is exactly when a reviewer wants to see them. The coupling it creates is
  real and belongs in this document rather than being designed away to keep a table tidy.
- **Make the two fitness modules stop importing `app`.** That means transcribing
  `AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` and `MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH` into the tests — which is the exact practice
  § Bounds are read from the constant forbids two sections below, and which
  `test_length_constants.py` exists to catch.
- **Say nothing and let the preamble stand.** It is the sentence a reader uses to decide
  whether a new fitness test may import the application. Wrong, it answers "no" to a question
  the tree answers "yes" to twice.

### The black box owns the database it runs against

# Tasks — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done

**Change:** CR-2609-823a. **From:** `spec/design/architecture.md` § The to-do list — where each
rule lives (the files and their writers), `spec/design/testing.md` § CR-2609-823a, the to-do list
and § Four file sets, disjoint (the tests, their cases and their authors),
`spec/design/data-model.md` § The revision that creates `todo_tasks`, `spec/design/api.md` § The
to-do list's endpoints and § The to-do list's refusals, `spec/design/ui/todo-list.md` and
`spec/design/ui/system-states.md`. A requirement written `R-n` below is `CR-2609-823a/R-n`.

## Reading this plan

**The waves are the profile's, derived by `sdd-engine skill_gate --list` from each member's
`after` in `.specconf/stack.json`.** Wave 1a is `build-tests-integration`, `build-tests-frontend`
and `build-tests-uat`. Wave 1b is `build-tests-unit` and `build-tests-e2e`, which the profile
orders after `build-tests-integration` because both import the corpus locator it writes. The RED
proof stands between wave 1 and wave 2. Wave 2 is `build-backend`, `build-migration`,
`build-frontend` and `build-platform`, which the profile orders after every test author. Each
member receives every task it owns, and does them in the order its `Depends on:` fields give.

**The fields.** `Files:` is the write allowlist of the task, and `Scope:` is the boundary row it
sits under (`set-boundary --from-design` recorded the boundary from the architecture fragment's
§ This change owns). `Depends on:` names only the tasks whose output this one reads or builds on.
`Parallel:` says what the task runs beside. `Must be red:` lists every case the task leaves
failing, and each is declared before the RED proof. `Green by design:` lists a planned case that
is already green, and correctly so, with the reason `green-by-design` records. `Turns green:`
lists a case that is red before the task starts and that the task's product turns green.
`Verification:` is the command, and what a pass looks like.

**How a declared case is spelled.** Every id below is `classname::name`, the form the junit
carries and the only one `declare-red` accepts.

- **pytest.** The classname is the module's dotted path, for example
  `tests.integration.test_todo_tasks_service`. A function listed with a bracket
  (`…::test_x[ascii_at_maximum]`) is parametrized, and its ids are the corpus's `case` field, or
  the ids this plan lists for the contract test. A function listed without a bracket is one
  collected case. Its variants (the four pairs of a marking, both orders of two writers, a
  marking, a correction and a deletion) live inside it and never in parameters, or its id would
  never be collected.
- **pytest-bdd.** All scenarios are collected in `e2e/suite/test_scenarios.py`, so the classname
  is `e2e.suite.test_scenarios`. The runner names a scenario `test_` followed by its title in
  lower case, with spaces as underscores and every other non-word character dropped. The titles
  are the ones `scenarios.md` gives, verbatim.
- **vitest.** The classname is the file's path relative to `frontend/`, the vitest root. The
  name is the test's own title, `[req:…]` included. A declared case stands at the top level of
  its file, because an enclosing `describe` prefixes the title with its own name and ` > `. It
  is one `it`, never an `it.each` whose title expands per row. A file vitest cannot load reports
  one case, `<path>::<path>`, and every case inside it goes uncollected.

**Red as itself.** A test author reaches a module wave 2 writes from inside the test or a
fixture, never at the top of the module: a failed top-level import un-collects every case in the
file, and a declared case the runner does not collect fails the gate (`spec/design/testing.md`
§ CR-2609-823a, "Red first"). No existing test is edited except where a task below names it.
